Enum Class TypedMarker

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<TypedMarker>
network.ike.support.enums.TypedMarker
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<TypedMarker>, Constable, ConstantBackedEnum, EnumDefinition
public enum TypedMarker extends Enum<TypedMarker> implements EnumDefinition
The IKE typed-marker family — the closed set of name-segments that the IKE property-naming convention recognizes inside an <G>__GA__<A> or <G>__GA__<A>__FACET property name.

The convention's one rule: __ is a separator between adjacent name-parts in a property name; trailing __ only appears when something follows. GA is a separator marker (the __ on both sides identify it as sitting between two name-parts — the groupId on the left and the artifactId on the right). VERSION and POLICY are terminal facet markers (no trailing __ because the XML structural terminator — > for declarations, } for references — closes the final segment).

The TypedMarker.Role distinguishes the two positions and selects the shape of the token returned by token() — __GA__ for separators, __VERSION or __POLICY for terminal facets. Future markers (e.g. GAV, BOM, SCOPE, PARENT, CLASSIFIER) slot in as additional enum constants without further design.

Replaced the U+00B7 (·) separator after IntelliJ's narrower [\w.\-]+-style property-resolver regex was found to reject the middle dot, breaking the ${G·A} chain and falsely flagging plugin parameters as unknown. The typed-marker family stays inside every resolver's identifier regex while remaining self-documenting and greppable (e.g. grep -E '__VERSION[>]'}). See IKE-Network/ike-issues#525.

Each rung carries a NAME_* mirror constant — the ConstantBackedEnum pattern — so the rung name is usable where a compile-time String constant is required; the class-load verify guard keeps the constants and mirrors in lockstep.

    • literalName

      public String literalName()
      The String literal carried by this constant.

      For TypedMarker the literal is the bare marker name (without __ boundaries) — e.g. "GA", "VERSION", "POLICY". Use token() to get the actual form that appears in a property name.

      Specified by:
      literalName in interface ConstantBackedEnum
      Returns:
      the literal, equal to the corresponding NAME_* mirror constant on the implementing enum

    • term

      public String term()
      The human-readable term this constant names.

      For TypedMarker the term and literalName() coincide — the marker name is both the vocabulary term and the literal that appears (between __ boundaries) in a property name.

      Specified by:
      term in interface EnumDefinition
      Returns:
      the term; never null or blank

    • role

      public TypedMarker.Role role()
      The position this marker occupies in a property name.
      Returns:
      TypedMarker.Role.SEPARATOR when the marker sits between two name-parts (rendered as __NAME__), TypedMarker.Role.FACET when the marker is terminal (rendered as __NAME)

    • token

      public String token()
      This marker as it appears in a property name. Separators are flanked by __ on both sides; terminal facets carry only the leading __. For example, GA.token() returns "__GA__" and POLICY.token() returns "__POLICY".
      Returns:
      the rendered token, suitable for string-concatenating into a property name
